small_guidance:
- The softmax+sigmoid epilogue is already cheap; the conv_transpose3d dominates. Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the existing kernel will not move fast_p meaningfully. If staying small, at least add autotune over num_warps ∈ {4,8} and num_stages ∈ {2,3} for BLOCK_C=64, but expected gain is <5%.
- Ensure the softmax kernel runs on a contiguous channels-first layout it already has; no further layout tweak helps until conv is replaced.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC-tile, input-spatial-tile) computes the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and atomically scatters into the output grid at `(n, oc, d*stride-pad+kd, h*stride-pad+kh, w*stride-pad+kw)`. Handle output_padding in bounds checks. This materializes the full (N, OC, D_out, H_out, W_out) tensor with the same FLOPs as the reference.
- Alternatively implement as gather-GEMM: for each output (n, oc, d_out, h_out, w_out) tile, accumulate over (ic, kd, kh, kw) the input element at the corresponding strided/padded location (skip when fractional). Tile shape `(BLOCK_M=64 over output spatial, BLOCK_N=32 over OC, BLOCK_K=16 over IC)` with num_warps=4, num_stages=2 fits SMEM safely.
- Fuse the softmax+sigmoid epilogue into the conv-transpose kernel: have the conv kernel write per-(n, spatial) channel vectors, then a second persistent kernel (or the same one with a barrier via separate launch) does the channel reduction. Since softmax reduces along OC=64, a single program per (n, d, h, w) holding all 64 channels in registers can fuse cleanly after the conv writes.
